newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Branson opposes British Airways-American Airlines link.
newsitem.headline: Branson opposes British Airways-American Airlines link.

text.p: Virgin Airlines Chairman Richard Branson said Monday that the European Commission should block an alliance between British Airways and AMR Corp.'s American Airlines as a threat to transatlantic competition.
Branson indicated that he would be leading a charge against the planned deal Tuesday at a commission hearing called to gather interested parties' views on the alliance.
"We are urging the commission to stop it," Branson said in Brussels, where he was preparing for the Tuesday hearing.
"The only way you could redresss the balance is, at least, to have another carrier with the same number of slots and (flight) frequencies," he said.
The closed-door hearing started Monday with British Airways and American Airlines defending their proposed alliance.
It followed weeks of angry exchanges between the Commission and the British authorities over who has the legal competence to examine the proposed transatlantic deal.
Others attending the hearing included representatives from Delta Air Lines, UAR Corpo.'s United Airlines, USAir and Continental Airlines.
European airlines, most of which are still state controlled, were being represented mainly by their governments.

Branson said BA and American would control nearly 80 percent of the routes between Britain and the United States. Virgin would be second with 10 percent of the traffic, followed by United Airlines with a 9 percent share.
